title: Count one buffer's bytes
starter:
let buffer_bytes (devices : int) (size : int) (elem : int) (written : bool) (stride : int) : int =
  if stride = 0 then devices * size * elem
  else begin
    let moved = ref (devices * size * elem) in
    if written then moved := devices * stride * elem;
    !moved
  end
hints: Look at the sharded case only. What does one device's copy in hold: the whole buffer or its shard?
A sharded copy in is `devices * stride * elem`, not `size`. A written buffer is copied in and then back out again, so its count is added to, not replaced.
`moved` starts at `devices * stride * elem`, and when `written` it becomes `moved + devices * stride * elem`: twice the copy in.

answer.code:
let buffer_bytes (devices : int) (size : int) (elem : int) (written : bool) (stride : int) : int =
  if stride = 0 then devices * size * elem
  else begin
    let moved = ref (devices * stride * elem) in
    if written then moved := !moved + devices * stride * elem;
    !moved
  end
answer.explain: Scatter copies every buffer to every device: the whole buffer when it is replicated, `stride` elements when it is sharded. Gather copies back only the written shards, the same `stride` elements per device. So a read-only shard costs `devices * stride * elem` bytes, a written one twice that, and a replicated buffer `devices * size * elem`.
